main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem} Let $P$ be a finitely generated virtually polycyclic group, and let $H$ be any finitely generated group. If $H$ and $P$ are quasi-isometric, then $H$ is virtually polycyclic. \end{theorem} \begin{corollary} If a finitely generated group $H$ is quasi-isometric to a lattice in a connected simply connected solvable Lie group, then a finite-index subgroup of $H$ is a uniform lattice in some connected simply connected solvable Lie group. \end{corollary} \begin{theorem}[Uniform bounded height] Let $G$ be a connected simply connected real-triangulable unimodular Lie group ... There is a finite subgroup $\A_G\leq\GL(W)$ such that, for every $K\geq1$ and $C\geq0$, there is a constant $B=B(G,K,C)$ ... Every $(K,C)$ self quasi-isometry $F$ of $G$ has an $A_F\in\A_G$ satisfying $\|\pi F(g)-\pi F(1)-A_F\pi(g)\|\leq B$.\end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: Virtual polycyclicity is a quasi-isometry invariant among all finitely generated groups (no solvability assumed on H). Equivalently (EFW lattice-recognition conjecture), groups QI to solvable Lie lattices are virtually uniform lattices in possibly different simply connected solvable Lie groups. The engine: every self-QI of a unimodular real-triangulable Lie group moves the canonical height coordinate by an element of a fixed finite linear group A_G up to a uniformly bounded error.

theorems: OAI.PolycyclicRecognition.group_recognition : GroupCoarseEquivalence P J -> IsVirtuallyPolycyclic P -> IsVirtuallyPolycyclic J /\ exists finite-index Gamma <= J isomorphic to a uniform lattice in some SimplyConnectedSolvableLieModel

OAI.PolycyclicRecognition.main_uniform_bounded_height : for R (simply connected solvable Lie group), any ProperChainMetric, a TriangularAdjoint basis, unimodular, W ~ HeightSpace, pi : R ->* Multiplicative W compatible with Exp, exists finite subgroup A <= (W ~L W) with forall K>=1, C>=0, exists B>=0, forall F : SelfQuasiIsometry K C, exists AF in A, forall g, ||pi(F g) - (pi(F 1) + AF(pi g))|| <= B

OAI.PolycyclicRecognition.lattice_recognition : finite-covolume lattice Lambda in S, GroupCoarseEquivalence Lambda J -> finite-index subgroup of J isomorphic to a uniform lattice in some SimplyConnectedSolvableLieModel
comparator.model: Coarse equivalence of f.g. groups encoded algebraically (bornologous maps with finite-set errors), equivalent to QI for word metrics. Lie models are bundled: finite-dimensional real manifold, LieGroup, T2, second countable, SimplyConnectedSpace, Group.IsSolvable. Height space = L / inf ker of the diagonal characters of a triangular adjoint basis. Uniform lattice = discrete + compact fundamental cover. Finite covolume = invariant probability on G/Lambda.

main_statement.match_check: Thm 1.1 + Cor 1.2: exact (group_recognition additionally includes the Dekimpe realization of J, i.e. the Cor 1.2 conclusion). Thm 1.4: exact or slightly stronger: the metric may be any proper compatible left-invariant metric with linear chains (paper: left-invariant Riemannian), W any normed space with a linear iso to the height quotient, pi any group hom agreeing with q o heightProjection on Exp; A is only asserted to be some finite subgroup (the paper's A_G is the explicit symmetry group of P; the Lean proof uses templateSymmetryGroup D, so the construction matches). Real-triangulability enters as existence of TriangularAdjoint. Universe restriction P J : Type (harmless). No definition_names, so comparator definitions are fixed by the statement file itself; I found no loophole at text level.
main_statement.formalized_vs_claimed: Formalized (claimed sorry-free): Thm 1.1, Cor 1.2 (finite-covolume version), Thm 1.4, plus the Dekimpe realization of the recognized group. Gromov's theorem comes from the external `gromov` package. Not separately formalized: nothing claimed in the paper appears missing; route differences listed under lean_structure.

proof_architecture.claim: Model reduction: P ~ uniform lattice Gamma in S ~QI real-triangulable unimodular G; H amenable; Gamma of type F and PD.
Lie coordinates: Cartan model q: N x| D -> G keeping N cap D; graded limit D_infinity; canonical height W and exact weight dilations.
Volume calculus: bracket-word exponent P(E), boxes, product schemes, switches; matching upper (path packing) and lower (fixed-sheet packing) bounds e^{rP(E)+o(r)}; finite symmetry group A_G of P.
Restricted products keep volume: polynomial image volume + backward recurrence.
Stationary slopes: compact pair space, H-bar^1 vanishing gives l=A pi (volume comparison), inverse coupling gives slope A^{-1}, hence A in A_G for every ergodic invariant measure.
Chart profiles of an arbitrary QI: occupation measures are invariant; limits satisfy convex-increment and segment-volume inequalities; affinity criterion makes them A pi z + b.
Neighbouring sheets share labels (reflection doubling) and offsets (cone-quotient Haar probes).
Remove randomness, stabilize across scales/basepoints: uniform sublinear height estimate with a single A_F; A_{Fbar}=A_F^{-1}.

Bounded error: ray-quotient boundary homeomorphisms; Haar volumes of boundary images record ell_beta(height); N-fiber variation bounded; Radon averaging gives ell_beta(pi F(d)) = ell_alpha(pi d)+O(1); Thm 1.4.

Recognition: labels give homomorphism H -> A_G; amenable correction tau; ker tau locally virtually nilpotent (Gromov) so H elementary amenable; Li FP_infinity, KMN type F + solvable, Li duality, Bieri => polycyclic finite-index subgroup; Cor 1.2 via Dekimpe.

route_differences_from_paper: Reduced cohomology: the paper cites Cornulier-Tessera 2020 Cor 1.9 for G; Lean proves vanishing of reduced H^1 for nilpotent groups (induction on class via center, Finiteness/NilpotentReducedCohomology.lean) and applies it to the Cartan factor D, identifying D-fixed vectors with G-fixed vectors by 'contracted root generation' (Geometry/CartanCocycleRestriction.lean).

Affinity criterion: the paper uses Hoermander's theorem for smoothness; Lean's LocalProfileAffinity 'does not assume a smooth profile or a hypoellipticity conclusion' (generator words + inverse function theorem).

Endgame: the paper uses KMN 2009; Lean final theorems go through Algebra/RecognitionWithoutKMN.lean ('Rational dimension, bounded finite subgroup orders, and duality after removing a finite normal subgroup').
Unimodularity of G: paper via metric Folner sets; Lean via lattice comparison (isMulRightInvariant_of_lattice_comparison).
Metric generality: the Lean height theorem accepts any proper compatible left-invariant metric with linear chains (coarse_pair_metric_change), not only Riemannian.

concerns: Unreviewed; quick search (2026-10-12) found no expert confirmation; 2025 literature (Grayevsky-Pallier) still lists the conjecture as open.

Prop 7.1 uses a diagonal argument with violating delta -> 0 and boundary convergence of profiles via equicontinuity (labels.tex:144-163); the facet co-location estimate is only o(r) after delta -> 0, a delicate order-of-limits point.

Many 'subexponential envelope' conventions (boxes.tex:163-172; uniformity.tex Remark 9.2) and order-of-choice subtleties (scheme fixed before restricting parameters, Remark 4.4); these are exactly where an informal proof could fail, so the Lean build is decisive.

Paper and Lean follow partly different routes (Cornulier-Tessera, Hoermander and KMN are not used in Lean). The paper's own uses of those theorems are therefore not certified; e.g. applying CT2020 Cor 1.9 to the L^2(X,mu) representation needs the WAP condition, which the paper asserts for Hilbert representations (true) - low risk.
Lean depends on the third-party `gromov` package (Gromov's theorem, 26.9k lines, Aug 2026); its correctness is part of the trust base and it must compile under the pinned toolchain.
Size: 262k Lean lines + gromov; any build failure reverts the claim to an unrefereed paper.
